L'expérience du cerf-volant de Franklin: Franklin's kite experiment (1752) is only known in detail through an account published fifteen years later by Joseph Priestley. In 1753, Georg Richmann, who was reproducing this kind of experiment in Saint Petersburg, was killed by lightning.

En 1825, Michael Faraday lance à la Roya: In 1825, Michael Faraday launched Christmas lectures for children at the Royal Institution. He gave nineteen series himself. They have been held every year since, except during World War II.

En 1945, l'ingénieur Percy Spencer trava: In 1945, engineer Percy Spencer is working on radar magnetrons at Raytheon and notices that a chocolate bar has melted in his pocket. He tries corn, which pops. The first microwave oven, in 1947, is almost two meters tall and weighs 340 kilos.

Le 9 septembre 1947, l'équipe du calcula: On September 9, 1947, the team of the Harvard Mark II calculator taped into its log a moth found in a relay: “First actual case of bug being found”. The joke works because the word already existed: Edison spoke of “bugs” in his inventions as early as 1878.

On attribue à Edison l'électrocution de: Edison is credited with electrocuting the elephant Topsy to discredit alternating current. It happened in 1903 at Coney Island, ten years after the war of the currents ended, and Edison had nothing to do with it. His company merely filmed the scene.
Master from transistor to computer. You surely have more than five at home.
« Je pense qu'il y a un marché mondial p: “I think there is a world market for maybe five computers.” The line is attributed to Thomas Watson, head of IBM, in 1943. Nobody has ever found it in a document from the time. The most famous failed predictions are often made up.

Vers 1747, Benjamin Franklin nomme « pos: Around 1747, Benjamin Franklin named the two kinds of electricity “positive” and “negative”, guessing which way the fluid flows. He had a fifty-fifty chance and got it wrong: electrons, discovered in 1897, go the other way. Conventional current keeps his choice.

Gustav Kirchhoff était encore étudiant,: Gustav Kirchhoff was still a student, in 1845, when he formulated his two circuit laws, for an exercise in Franz Neumann's seminar at Königsberg. The work became his thesis.

En 1858, le message de la reine Victoria: In 1858, Queen Victoria's message to President Buchanan, 98 words, took 16 hours to cross the Atlantic. Three weeks later, the cable died, fried by 2,000 volts. The 1866 one would carry 8 words a minute.

To catch electric eels, they drove about thirty horses into a pond: the fish attacked and wore themselves out. Two horses, stunned, drowned; the tired eels were caught with harpoons.

In China, the compass "points south". Around 1044, the Wujing Zongyao describes an iron fish floated on a bowl of water; it was magnetised by heating it and letting it cool in the right direction.

Dans sa Lettre sur l'aimant de 1269, Pie: In his Letter on the Magnet of 1269, Peter of Maricourt proposed a toothed wheel that a magnet would turn forever, by attracting then repelling its teeth. It never turned.

La terrella de Gilbert est une boule tai: Gilbert's terrella is a ball carved from lodestone. A needle placed on it behaves like a compass on Earth: it stays flat at the equator and plunges towards the poles. Hence his conclusion of 1600: the Earth is a magnet.

En août 1753, à Saint-Pétersbourg, Georg: In August 1753, in Saint Petersburg, Georg Wilhelm Richmann repeated the lightning experiment and died, apparently struck by ball lightning. Franklin had never seen his kite struck: the charge came from a nearby cloud.

Avant d'être physicien, Coulomb est offi: Before being a physicist, Coulomb was a military engineer. Sent to Martinique, he directed the building of the new Fort Bourbon, a project that kept him there from 1764 to 1772. His law of electricity came only in 1785.

À la mort de Guglielmo Marconi, en 1937,: At Guglielmo Marconi's death, in 1937, radio transmitters around the world observed two minutes of silence, at 6 pm, on the day of his funeral.
